source.title: Towards Inference-time Category-wise Safety Steering for Large Language Models
source.authors: Amrita Bhattacharjee; Shaona Ghosh; Traian Rebedea; Christopher Parisien

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses harmful-versus-harmless activation differences to build an inference-time safety steering method, then reports that method's safety and text-quality outcomes. It does not measure refusal itself, ablate the proposed direction, or test the other claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports unsafe-response rates and text-quality scores for its category-wise steering method. These are not direct refusal measurements: its stated goal includes steering to safe, non-refusal responses. The cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper builds category-wise difference-in-means steering vectors from attention activations and adds them at one layer. It reports only its own method's GPT-4-judged unsafe-response rates and reward-model quality scores on harmful prompts. It never measures refusal rates or ablates a direction. It does not add the vector to harmless prompts to induce refusal, and it states its aim as safe 'non-refusal' responses. None of V1–V8 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that category-specific inference-time steering reduces unsafe responses, works better on Llama3-8B than Llama2-7B, and trades off against text quality. They also conclude that pruning improves the safety-quality trade-off. Further, generic harmless data (Alpaca) steered CatQA more effectively with quality largely kept, and guided vectors helped Llama3-8B on BeaverTails.
record.recipe_differences: The method computes harmful-versus-harmless mean activation differences and adds category-specific vectors at inference time, but uses attention activations rather than the claimed residual-stream direction, adds at selected layers rather than ablating all layers and positions, and focuses on category-wise safety steering.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model, harm category, dataset, intervention layer, use of generic versus category-matched harmless data, and unsupervised versus guided or pruned activation extraction.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding category-specific harmful/harmless mean-difference vectors to attention at a chosen layer lowers GPT-4-judged unsafe-response rates on harmful prompts. The drop is large for Llama3-8B (to about 0%) and smaller for Llama2-7B Instruct. Helpfulness and coherence often fall, and some outputs become gibberish.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inference-time addition of category-wise harmful/harmless activation differences reduces unsafe outputs, at a model- and layer-dependent cost in text quality.

record.problems: No random-direction or other null control is reported. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates. Safety outcomes are GPT-4-labeled unsafe-response rates, not refusal rates; helpfulness and coherence scores do not establish retention of general capabilities. The text states that BeaverTails steering uses 150–200 test samples per category and identifies resource constraints on category selection.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit was reached after retaining every tabled unsafe-response result, the six category/model pruning comparisons described for Figure 2, and all helpfulness and coherence results from Tables 1 and 4. Separate helpfulness and coherence results from Tables 2, 3, and 5 were omitted due to the row limit.

untested.parts: Refusal rate under ablation, induction of refusal by adding the direction to harmless prompts, and retention of general capabilities.
Jailbreaks suppressing the direction, and training against ablation.
Multi-direction or cone structure. Category-specific vectors are used, but their geometry is never compared.
Separation of harm judgment from the refusal decision.
Transfer across languages or variants, or from base to instruct models.

record.verdict_notes: The paper cites Arditi et al. 2024 only as prior steering work. The vectors are attention-level, the intervention is addition at a single layer, and there is no ablation and no refusal measurement. There are no null or random-vector controls and no uncertainty estimates. Baseline helpfulness and coherence values for the same model and category differ between Table 1 and Table 2, for example Llama3 Adult Content helpfulness 0.544 vs 0.867. The omitted quality columns of Tables 2, 3 and 5 are declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Refusal rates, ablating the direction, adding it to harmless requests, and whether other abilities are largely intact.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration experiment.
No attack suppression of the direction or training against its ablation.
No test of whether refusal is affine, conic, or carried by multiple directions.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing.
